structured.approach: I read the TSK-07 Frontend task in feat.tasks to see what the change touches: one render helper, the version in package.json and the test file, with no transport. I checked that against the tool view for the restricted permission table, which says no secrets are required or granted for ap_portal. I then read the ap_portal source (index.js), the CI script (ci.mjs), package.json and the full test file (tests/portal.test.js) to confirm that nothing reads a secret. Required and granted secrets match (none on either side), so I raised no access request and wrote task.secrets_scope in full with names only.

claims.text: The Frontend task TSK-07 (STORY-07) changes only src/ap_portal/index.js, package.json (version only) and tests/portal.test.js in ap_portal.
TSK-07 depends only on the CT-1 field list, and the design adds no transport layer, so the frontend task calls no service.
No secrets are required or granted for the ap_portal repository according to the permission table.
ap_portal's package.json declares no dependencies, so no package registry token is needed.
The current ap_portal source reads no environment variable and calls no external service.
The CI script sets only NODE_PATH to 'src' on top of the process environment and reads no secret.
The portal tests load only node:test, node:assert and ap_portal, and call formatAmount and renderAgingSummary on literal values without reading any environment variable.
Required and granted secrets match (none), so no access request is raised and the task can go ahead.

structured.summary: I read tests/portal.test.js in full this time, so the claim that cites it is now backed by what I read. The Frontend task for FEAT-ZD-48600 (TSK-07, ap_portal) needs no secrets in local, dev or main, and the permission table grants none, so no access request is needed. I rewrote task.secrets_scope.md in full with names only and kept the tool-results note the spine had added to the file. The file says FE-02 runs again if a later change adds a transport, an external API call or a dependency that needs a token.
